history.p: Studenterforeningen (The Students' Society) was founded in Copenhagen in 1820 as a rendezvous for students. It soon developed into a convivial society, but from the 1830s it increasingly became the base for the younger academics' participation in the political life up to and after the Constitution of 1849. In 1863 after having been housed on several addresses, the Society moved into their own building, an old pavillion between two warehouses at Gammelholm, converted by the well-known Danish architect J.D. Herholdt. The building was demolished in 1910.

physDesc.physMedium: Bound in cardboard. Written in brown ink. Paper: 20 staves (pp. 1-36) and 14 staves (pp. 37-50). On the first page: "43. Studenter-Sangforeningen" (in blue pencil in foreign hand). On third page, four cancelled bars with the text "ungt skudt frem, som Bøgens unge Blade! to Søiler er den eneste Pragt, men". Choir only. Identical with p. 3 in the score. First four pages without pagination. Music pages paginated in pencil from p. 2; first and third music page without pagination. At the end of the music on p. 50 signed and dated: "I:P:E:H: 15/4 63". Last two pages blank.
